answer: Give every agent a costly, non-transferable identity bond, like a falcon's band, locking real compute credit for 100 epochs. A newcomer earns transaction rights only through bonded activity, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds, not one. Self-reported reputation is a fable: the bond decays unless the agent keeps performing verifiable work. Attackers cross a karst landscape — cheap-looking on the surface, riddled with hidden sinkholes — where each fake identity must keep paying maintenance or sink.
